text: Agra is a historic city on the Yamuna and part of the Delhi-Agra-Jaipur Golden Triangle. Its Mughal heritage is reflected in its monuments and bazaars.
Agra's three UNESCO World Heritage Sites are the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri, according to Incredible India.
The Incredible India guide lists Agra Airport (AGR), Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL) and Agra City Railway Station (AGA) for travel to Agra.
Incredible India recommends spring (February to April) or autumn (September to November) for Agra, describing the weather in those periods as pleasant.
General India travel guidance: respect local dress codes and customs, particularly at religious sites and in rural areas.
General India travel guidance warns that scammers, pickpockets and ticket touts target visitors in tourist areas. Check ticket sellers and agents before paying.
General India travel advice recommends following local authority guidance, keeping belongings secure on public transport and in crowds, and using emergency number 112 when needed.

Varanasi, also called Kashi or Banaras, is a historic city and a major spiritual destination on the Ganga. Incredible India describes October to March as the pleasant season for exploring its riverfront and old city.
The Varanasi guide identifies the ghats and old city as central experiences and recommends nearby Sarnath for visitors interested in the city's spiritual history.

Varanasi is served by Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport (VNS) and Varanasi Junction Railway Station (BSB). The official guide also lists Banaras, Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction and Kashi stations.
Incredible India describes October to March as the most pleasant time to explore Varanasi, including its ghats, old city and river.
General India travel guidance: respect local dress codes and customs, particularly at religious sites and in rural areas.
General India travel guidance warns that scammers, pickpockets and ticket touts target visitors in tourist areas. Check ticket sellers and agents before paying.
General India travel advice recommends following local authority guidance, keeping belongings secure on public transport and in crowds, and using emergency number 112 when needed.
